To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

performance information should be: * Relevant - to the needs of stakeholders; * Reliable - in that stakeholders can trust the information they receive and use it to make informed decisions; * Comparable - so that stakeholders can make comparisons with other services and other organisations; and * Understandable - to all stakeholders.

the performance measurement needs for stakeholders are diverse, and that a stakeholder-based approach to performance measurement can be used to develop a performance measurement information portfolio that meets the needs of a wide range of stakeholders.

the approach to performance measurement for stakeholders was useful, allowing services in the public sector to develop an information package that met the performance information needs and judgements of diverse stakeholders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology to identify the performance measurement needs for stakeholders in the public sector and to identify the information required to address these needs.
the development of a stakeholder approach to performance measurement.
the development of a performance measurement framework for local authorities that is responsive to the needs of a wide range of stakeholders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach was a valuable way of identifying the performance information needs for stakeholders and of developing a portfolio of information that would meet those needs.
the performance measurement approach was useful in helping to develop an information system to meet the performance needs of stakeholders.
the approach has been found useful in identifying the information needs of a wide range of stakeholders and the information that would be needed to satisfy those needs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development of performance measurement information portfolios for services is a useful and practical way of identifying and responding to the performance measurement needs and information requirements of stakeholders.

the approach was found useful, allowing the services to identify the judgements about the performance that each group of stakeholders wanted to make and to identify the key information that would be required.

the approach is a valuable one for services to consider, and one which is likely to be of particular value to those services which are subject to multiple performance measurement demands from a range of stakeholders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
performance information needs are not uniform across stakeholders and that services need to tailor their performance reporting to the needs of different stakeholder groups.
stakeholders are likely to have very different views on the relative importance of different performance measures.
performance measurement systems should be developed to meet stakeholder needs, rather than being developed in isolation and then presented to stakeholders for comment.
